1	# Release & Stub-Ascend Reference
2	
3	> **Scope:** the crate version lifecycle, the stub-ascend recipe, the two
4	> publish deadlocks it has caused (SMA-321, SMA-346), and the release-plz
5	> `git/refs` 403 with the release gap report (SMA-745).
6	> This runbook is **not** linked from the public mdBook — it lives standalone under
7	> `docs/runbooks/` to avoid linkcheck coupling. It holds the *rationale and incident
8	> history*; the operative rules stay in `CLAUDE.md`.
9	
10	## Version lifecycle
11	
12	**Per-crate version is the one exception**, with a two-state lifecycle:
13	
14	1. **Stub state — `version = "0.0.0"` + `publish = false` in Cargo.toml + `release = false` block in `release-plz.toml`.** Every stub was pre-published once to crates.io at `0.0.0` during SMA-385 to claim the name and satisfy the facade's optional-dep resolver. After that pre-publish, cargo refuses to republish (the per-crate `publish = false`); release-plz ignores them entirely (the `release = false`).
15	2. **Released state — bumped to a real version (≥ `0.1.0`)** after the first real public-API ticket lands. The 4-step ascend recipe:
16	   - Bump `version = "0.0.0"` → `"0.1.0"` in the crate's `Cargo.toml`.
17	   - Remove `publish = false` from that `Cargo.toml`.
18	   - Remove the crate's `[[package]] … release = false` block from `release-plz.toml`.
19	   - Land as one `chore(release): SMA-### lift stage-1 gates for <crate>` commit on the feature branch alongside the implementation. release-plz handles the first crates.io publish on CI.
20	
21	   The 4-step recipe applies to **stubs ascending from `0.0.0`**. The ten already-released crates (`-core`, facade, `-macros`, `-providers-openai`, `-providers-anthropic`, `-providers-bedrock`, `-sessions-sqlite`, `-runtime-tokio`, `-mcp`, `-tools`) ship through release-plz's normal flow — no manual ritual needed for their future bumps. The historical chain of `chore(release): … escape release-plz 0.0.0 trap …` commits in the git log (SMA-317/347/350/372/382) is pre-Stage-1 archaeology and won't recur.
22	
23	## Caveat 1 — same-PR core API needs a core bump (SMA-321)
24	
25	**Caveat — when the ascending crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too** (a 5th step). `cargo publish --verify` builds the ascending crate's tarball against the **registry** core (the `path` is stripped at publish), so if crates.io `core` lacks the new API the publish fails with `failed to verify package tarball`, and release-plz's combined job (SMA-351) aborts before its release-PR step — a deadlock, since `core` never gets its auto bump (a squashed `feat(<ascending-crate>)` commit attributes nothing to `core`). Fix: in the same PR, also bump `paigasus-helikon-core` (patch for additive/non-breaking-behind-`#[non_exhaustive]`, e.g. `0.2.0` → `0.2.1`) and its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin + CHANGELOG. release-plz then publishes `core` first, then the ascending crate verifies against the fresh `core` (dependency-ordered publish). Diagnosed in SMA-321: PR #45's release failed against the stale `core` `0.2.0`; PR #46 (`chore(release)` bumping `core` to `0.2.1`) cleared it.
26	
27	## Caveat 2 — the manual core bump defeats the facade cascade (SMA-346)
28	
29	**Second-order caveat — the manual core bump silently defeats `dependencies_update`, so the facade drifts.** `release-plz.toml` sets `dependencies_update = true`, which is *supposed* to cascade: when a sibling's version changes, release-plz bumps the facade's `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and gives the facade a patch bump. But that cascade only runs when **release-plz itself performs the sibling bump**. The same-PR manual bump above means the sibling version is already at target when the PR merges, so release-plz just publishes it and never runs the dependent-bump step — the facade (`paigasus-helikon`) is left untouched and stops tracking. Consequence: the facade stays at its old version with stale published dep reqs (e.g. after SMA-346, facade `0.2.0` still requested `paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio = ^0.0.0`, so the new runner-boundary surface was unreachable through the facade's `runtime-tokio` feature). **Fix: in any PR that uses the same-PR manual bump, ALSO bump the facade** (patch: `version` in `crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` + its `[workspace.dependencies]` self-pin + CHANGELOG) so it republishes with current sibling reqs. Diagnosed after SMA-346: PRs #48/#49 shipped `core 0.2.3` + `runtime-tokio 0.1.1` but left facade `0.2.0`; PR #50 (`chore(release)` bumping facade to `0.2.1`) cleared it. NB: feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.
30	
31	## A red release-plz run with 403 on `git/refs` (SMA-745)
32	
33	**Symptom.** A `release-plz.yml` run fails with `403 Forbidden` and an empty body on `POST /repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs`. The failed call can create a release branch or a tag. On 2026-10-30, two runs failed this way. One run published `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 to crates.io and then failed to create the tag. The crate had no tag and no GitHub release.
34	
35	**Cause.** GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes on `main`. The token needs the `workflow` permission for this. In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` merged while the run was in progress. We measured this on 2026-10-31 with an OAuth token that had no `workflow` scope. We did not use the App token. The same call, ref name and token gave different results:
36	
37	| Target commit | Position | Result |
38	| -- | -- | -- |
39	| A commit behind a workflow change on `main` | behind `main` | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
40	| The tip of `main` | tip of `main` | ref created |
41	
42	We measured only the 404 with the OAuth token. The App token got 403 in the incident runs. We think that both are refusals of the same check. The fix below uses the App token with `workflows: write`. That token is **not tested yet**, because the App private key exists only in Actions secrets. The first `release-plz` run after the merge that overlaps a workflow merge is the first real evidence. The gap report (below) catches a failure if the fix is not enough.
43	
44	**Fix.** The `actions/create-github-app-token` step in `release-plz.yml` requests `permission-workflows: write`. The paigasusbot App (ID 3742291) has `Workflows: Read and write`. If the installation loses this permission, the token step fails. Then restore the permission in the App settings and accept it on the installation.
45	
46	**The `release` environment.** The extra power of the token has a risk. A leaked token can push a branch that has a new `on: push` workflow. Such a workflow can read repository secrets. The `release-plz` job therefore sets `environment: release`. This environment allows only the `main` branch. It has no required reviewers, so the release stays automatic. `scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` creates the environment. Set `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as **environment** secrets of `release`, by hand. Do not set them as repository secrets. A repository-level copy would be readable from any branch.
47	
48	**The gap report.** Each `release-plz` run ends with the step "report release gaps". It runs `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`. For each publishable crate, it checks the version at the run commit. It reports a gap when crates.io lists the version but the tag `<package>-v<version>` or the non-draft GitHub release is missing. The script only reports. It does not repair. The step has three results:
49	
50	| Result | Exit code | Meaning |
51	| -- | -- | -- |
52	| No gaps | 0 | Every published version has a tag and a release. |
53	| Gap | 1 | At least one version is published without a tag or a release. The step is red, also when release-plz was green. |
54	| Could not check | 2 | An error or an unexpected response stopped a check. On a green release step, this is a `::warning::` and the step exits 0. On a red release step, the step stays red. |
55	
56	"Could not check" is never "no gaps". A network error, an API error, an empty package list and a `git_tag_name`, `git_tag_enable` or `git_release_enable` key in `release-plz.toml` all give "could not check". The report lists the reason for each item. To run the report locally, use `GH_TOKEN=REDACTED auth token) bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`.
57	
58	**Recovery.** The step summary shows the commands for each gap. In general form, with `<tag>` as `<package>-v<version>`:
59	
60	If the tag already exists and only the release is missing, skip steps 2 to 4.
61	
62	1. Give your `gh` token the `workflow` scope: `gh auth refresh -s workflow`.
63	2. Look in the failed run log for the annotated tag object that release-plz made. Check it: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/tags/<tag-sha> --jq '{tag, sha: .object.sha}'`. The tag name and the object SHA must match the release commit.
64	3. Create the ref: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs -f ref=refs/tags/<tag> -f sha=<tag-sha>`.
65	4. If the call fails because the tag object does not exist, make a new annotated tag object at the release commit with `POST /git/tags`. Then repeat step 3 with its SHA. The release commit is the commit that bumped the version. The gap can come from an earlier run, so the commit of the current run can be wrong.
66	5. GitHub returns 404 for a draft release. Look for a draft with this tag. `gh release list` shows only 30 releases, so use the API with pagination: `gh api --paginate "repos/<repo>/releases?per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select(.tag_name == "<tag>" and .draft == true) | .id'`. If one exists, publish it with `gh release edit <tag> --draft=false --latest=false`. Without `--latest=false`, GitHub marks the published release as "Latest". Do not make a second release.
67	6. Else create the release: `gh release create <tag> --verify-tag --latest=false --title <tag> --notes-file <file>`. Put the CHANGELOG section of that version in the file.
68	7. Remove the extra scope: `gh auth refresh -r workflow`.
69	8. Run the gap report again. It must say "no gaps".
70	
71	**Rule.** A red `release-plz` run can still have published crates. Do not assume that nothing shipped. Read the gap report first. Then check crates.io, the tags and the releases.
72	
73	**Rollout order for the SMA-745 change.** Run `sh scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` and set the three environment secrets before the merge. If the `release` environment does not exist when the workflow first runs, GitHub creates it without a branch policy. Thus the script must run before the merge. Merge only when no `release-plz` run is queued or in progress. After the first run on `main`, run `gh secret list --env release`. Make sure that it shows `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`. Then delete the three repository-level secrets. For a rollback, revert the workflow change. Restore the repository-level secrets before you do this.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# check-release-gaps.sh — find published crate versions that have no git tag or
3	# no GitHub release (SMA-745).
4	#
5	# A release-plz run can publish a crate to crates.io and then fail before it
6	# makes the tag or the GitHub release. This script finds that gap. It reports
7	# only. It does not repair a gap.
8	#
9	# For each workspace package whose `publish` field is not [], the script checks
10	# the package version at this commit:
11	#   1. crates.io lists the version (a yanked version also counts). If not, the
12	#      version is not published and there is no gap.
13	#   2. The tag <package>-v<version> exists (exact match).
14	#   3. A GitHub release that is not a draft exists for that tag.
15	#
16	# Results and exit codes:
17	#   0  no gaps.
18	#   1  at least one gap (with or without "could not check" items).
19	#   2  "could not check", no gap. When RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME is "success", the
20	#      script writes a ::warning:: and exits 0 instead.
21	# An error, an unexpected response or an empty package list is always "could
22	# not check". It is never "no gaps", and never "missing".
23	#
24	# Environment inputs:
25	#   GH_TOKEN               token for `gh` (read access to refs and releases).
26	#   GITHUB_REPOSITORY      owner/name. Default: SMK1085/paigasus-helikon.
27	#   RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA  path to `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1`
28	#                          output. If unset, the script runs that command.
29	#   RELEASE_GAPS_CONFIG    path to release-plz.toml. Default: <repo>/release-plz.toml.
30	#   RELEASE_GAPS_SLEEP     seconds between crates.io requests. Default: 1.
31	#   RELEASE_GAPS_DEADLINE  time limit for all checks, in seconds from the script
32	#                          start. Default: 210. When the limit is reached, the
33	#                          script stops the checks, puts each crate that it did
34	#                          not check under "could not check" and writes the
35	#                          report. The step `timeout-minutes` is only a backstop.
36	#   RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME   success, failure or cancelled. Unset means failure.
37	#   GITHUB_SHA             commit for the recovery text. Default: HEAD.
38	#   GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY    if set, the report is also appended to this file.
39	#
40	# Run locally: GH_TOKEN=REDACTED auth token) bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh
41	
42	set -euo pipefail
43	
44	repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
45	repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-SMK1085/paigasus-helikon}"
46	config="${RELEASE_GAPS_CONFIG:-${repo_root}/release-plz.toml}"
47	pause="${RELEASE_GAPS_SLEEP:-1}"
48	deadline="${RELEASE_GAPS_DEADLINE:-210}"
49	outcome="${RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME:-failure}"
50	if [[ -n "${GITHUB_SHA:-}" ]]; then
51	  sha="${GITHUB_SHA}"
52	else
53	  sha="$(git -C "${repo_root}" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo HEAD)"
54	fi
55	# crates.io refuses the default curl User-Agent with 403.
56	user_agent="paigasus-helikon-release-gaps (https://github.com/${repo})"
57	
58	tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
59	trap 'rm -rf "${tmp}"' EXIT
60	
61	gaps="${tmp}/gaps.md"        # one block per gap, for the report.
62	unknown="${tmp}/unknown.md"  # one line per "could not check" item.
63	: > "${gaps}"
64	: > "${unknown}"
65	gap_count=0
66	checked=0
67	
68	# Record an item that the script could not check.
69	#   could_not_check <text>
70	could_not_check() {
71	  printf -- '- could not check: %s\n' "$1" >> "${unknown}"
72	}
73	
74	# Print the report to stdout and to the job summary, then exit.
75	finish() {
76	  local report="${tmp}/report.md" unknown_count status
77	  unknown_count="$(grep -c '^- ' "${unknown}" || true)"
78	  {
79	    echo "## Release gap report"
80	    echo
81	    echo "Repository \`${repo}\`, commit \`${sha}\`."
82	    echo
83	    if [[ "${gap_count}" == 0 && "${unknown_count}" == 0 ]]; then
84	      echo "Result: no gaps. ${checked} published package version(s) checked."
85	    fi
86	    if [[ "${gap_count}" != 0 ]]; then
87	      echo "### Gaps: ${gap_count} published version(s) without tag or release"
88	      echo
89	      echo "The recovery commands need a token with the \`workflow\` scope:"
90	      echo "\`gh auth refresh -s workflow\`. Remove the scope after the recovery:"
91	      echo "\`gh auth refresh -r workflow\`."
92	      echo
93	      cat "${gaps}"
94	    fi
95	    if [[ "${unknown_count}" != 0 ]]; then
96	      echo "### Could not check: ${unknown_count} item(s)"
97	      echo
98	      echo "These items are not known to be correct. Do not read them as \"no gaps\"."
99	      echo
100	      cat "${unknown}"
101	      echo
102	    fi
103	  } > "${report}"
104	
105	  cat "${report}"
106	  # A failed write must not change the exit code: exit 1 means "gap".
107	  if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
108	    if ! cat "${report}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}" 2>/dev/null; then
109	      echo "::warning::cannot write job summary"
110	    fi
111	  fi
112	
113	  if [[ "${gap_count}" != 0 ]]; then
114	    echo "::error::release gaps: ${gap_count} published version(s) without tag or release — see the job summary"
115	    status=1
116	  elif [[ "${unknown_count}" != 0 ]]; then
117	    if [[ "${outcome}" == "success" ]]; then
118	      echo "::warning::release gap report: could not check ${unknown_count} item(s) — see the job summary"
119	      status=0
120	    else
121	      status=2
122	    fi
123	  else
124	    status=0
125	  fi
126	  exit "${status}"
127	}
128	
129	# Run `gh api --include <path>` with a time limit. Set `http_status` to the
130	# status code from the first output line ("" if there is none), and write the
131	# response body to the file `${tmp}/gh-body`. The gh exit code is ignored: gh
132	# exits non-zero for every HTTP error, and only the status tells a 404 from an
133	# auth error.
134	#   gh_get <api-path>
135	gh_get() {
136	  local out="${tmp}/gh-out"
137	  : > "${out}"
138	  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
139	    timeout 30 gh api --include "$1" > "${out}" 2>"${tmp}/gh-err" || true
140	  else
141	    gh api --include "$1" > "${out}" 2>"${tmp}/gh-err" || true
142	  fi
143	  tr -d '\r' < "${out}" > "${out}.lf"
144	  http_status="$(head -n 1 "${out}.lf" | sed -n 's#^HTTP/[0-9.]* \([0-9][0-9][0-9]\).*$#\1#p')"
145	  # The body starts after the first empty line.
146	  awk 'body { print } !body && $0 == "" { body = 1 }' "${out}.lf" > "${tmp}/gh-body"
147	}
148	
149	if ! [[ "${deadline}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
150	  could_not_check "RELEASE_GAPS_DEADLINE is \`${deadline}\`, not a whole number of seconds."
151	  finish
152	fi
153	
154	# --- tag format guard ----------------------------------------------------------
155	# The script assumes the default tag format <package>-v<version>. It must not
156	# guess another format, so a setting that changes tags or releases stops it.
157	if [[ ! -r "${config}" ]]; then
158	  could_not_check "cannot read \`${config}\`, so the tag format is not known."
159	  finish
160	fi
161	for key in git_tag_name git_tag_enable git_release_enable; do
162	  if grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*${key}[[:space:]]*=" "${config}"; then
163	    could_not_check "\`${config}\` sets \`${key}\`. This script knows only the default tag format \`<package>-v<version>\` with tags and releases enabled. Update the script for the new setting."
164	  fi
165	done
166	if [[ -s "${unknown}" ]]; then
167	  finish
168	fi
169	
170	# --- package list ----------------------------------------------------------------
171	metadata="${RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA:-}"
172	if [[ -z "${metadata}" ]]; then
173	  metadata="${tmp}/metadata.json"
174	  if ! cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 \
175	      --manifest-path "${repo_root}/Cargo.toml" > "${metadata}" 2>"${tmp}/cargo-err"; then
176	    could_not_check "\`cargo metadata\` failed: $(head -c 300 "${tmp}/cargo-err" | tr '\n' ' ')"
177	    finish
178	  fi
179	fi
180	if [[ ! -r "${metadata}" ]]; then
181	  could_not_check "cannot read the metadata file \`${metadata}\`."
182	  finish
183	fi
184	packages="${tmp}/packages.tsv"
185	# One line per package: name, version, crate directory relative to the
186	# workspace root (absolute if it is not below the root).
187	if ! jq -r '
188	    .workspace_root as $root
189	    | .packages[]
190	    | select(.publish != [])
191	    | (.manifest_path | sub("/Cargo\\.toml$"; "")) as $dir
192	    | [ .name, .version,
193	        (if ($dir | startswith($root + "/")) then $dir[($root | length) + 1:] else $dir end)
194	      ]
195	    | @tsv' "${metadata}" > "${packages}" 2>"${tmp}/jq-err"; then
196	  could_not_check "cannot parse the metadata file \`${metadata}\`: $(head -c 300 "${tmp}/jq-err" | tr '\n' ' ')"
197	  finish
198	fi
199	if [[ ! -s "${packages}" ]]; then
200	  could_not_check "the metadata has no publishable packages (every package has \`publish = []\`), so nothing was checked."
201	  finish
202	fi
203	
204	# --- per package -----------------------------------------------------------------
205	first_request=1
206	deadline_reached=0
207	while IFS=$'\t' read -r name version dir <&3; do
208	  tag="${name}-v${version}"
209	
210	  # Overall time limit. In an API outage, one crate can take about 81 s, so the
211	  # step time limit can stop the script before it writes a report. SECONDS is
212	  # the time since the script started (bash 3.2 has it too).
213	  if [[ "${deadline_reached}" == 0 && "${SECONDS}" -ge "${deadline}" ]]; then
214	    deadline_reached=1
215	  fi
216	  if [[ "${deadline_reached}" == 1 ]]; then
217	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: deadline reached (RELEASE_GAPS_DEADLINE=${deadline} s), so the script did not check this crate."
218	    continue
219	  fi
220	
221	  # crates.io. Wait between requests (crawler policy: 1 request per second).
222	  if [[ "${first_request}" == 0 ]]; then
223	    sleep "${pause}"
224	  fi
225	  first_request=0
226	  body="${tmp}/crate.json"
227	  : > "${body}"
228	  curl_rc=0
229	  code="$(curl -sS --max-time 20 -A "${user_agent}" -o "${body}" -w '%{http_code}' \
230	    "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/${name}" 2>"${tmp}/curl-err")" || curl_rc=$?
231	  if [[ "${curl_rc}" != 0 ]]; then
232	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the crates.io request failed (curl exit ${curl_rc}, HTTP ${code:-none}): $(head -c 200 "${tmp}/curl-err" | tr '\n' ' ')"
233	    continue
234	  fi
235	  if [[ "${code}" != "200" ]]; then
236	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: crates.io returned HTTP ${code} for the crate."
237	    continue
238	  fi
239	  if ! listed="$(jq -r --arg v "${version}" '
240	      if (.versions | type) != "array" then error("no versions list")
241	      elif any(.versions[]; (type != "object") or ((.num | type) != "string")) then "malformed"
242	      else ([.versions[].num] | index($v) != null)
243	      end' "${body}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
244	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: crates.io returned HTTP 200, but the body has no readable versions list."
245	    continue
246	  fi
247	  # An entry without a string `num` can be the version under check. Then the
248	  # version looks unpublished, and that gives a false "no gaps".
249	  if [[ "${listed}" == "malformed" ]]; then
250	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: crates.io returned HTTP 200, but the versions list is malformed (an entry has no string \`num\`)."
251	    continue
252	  fi
253	  # A truncated list can omit the version and make a published version look
254	  # unpublished. The list length must equal crate.num_versions. If jq fails,
255	  # the two sentinels are different, so the check fails and the crate goes to
256	  # "could not check".
257	  counts="$(jq -r '"\(.versions | length) \(.crate.num_versions | if type == "number" then . else "missing" end)"' \
258	    "${body}" 2>/dev/null || echo "unreadable-list unreadable-count")"
259	  listed_count="${counts%% *}"
260	  total_count="${counts##* }"
261	  if [[ "${listed_count}" == "unreadable-list" ]]; then
262	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: crates.io returned HTTP 200, but the version count or crate.num_versions is not readable."
263	    continue
264	  fi
265	  if [[ "${listed_count}" != "${total_count}" ]]; then
266	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: crates.io lists ${listed_count} version(s), but crate.num_versions is ${total_count}. The versions list can be incomplete."
267	    continue
268	  fi
269	  if [[ "${listed}" != "true" ]]; then
270	    # Not published, so a missing tag or release is not a gap.
271	    continue
272	  fi
273	  checked=$((checked + 1))
274	
275	  missing=""
276	
277	  # Tag. The singular "ref" endpoint matches the exact name only.
278	  gh_get "repos/${repo}/git/ref/tags/${tag}"
279	  case "${http_status}" in
280	    200) ;;
281	    404) missing="tag" ;;
282	    "") could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the tag request for \`${tag}\` gave no HTTP status." ;;
283	    *) could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the tag request for \`${tag}\` returned HTTP ${http_status}." ;;
284	  esac
285	
286	  # Release.
287	  gh_get "repos/${repo}/releases/tags/${tag}"
288	  case "${http_status}" in
289	    200)
290	      draft="$(jq -r 'if (.draft | type) == "boolean" then .draft else error("no draft field") end' \
291	        "${tmp}/gh-body" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
292	      case "${draft}" in
293	        false) ;;
294	        true) missing="${missing:+${missing} }draft-release" ;;
295	        *) could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the release request for \`${tag}\` returned HTTP 200, but the body has no readable \`draft\` field." ;;
296	      esac
297	      ;;
298	    404) missing="${missing:+${missing} }release" ;;
299	    "") could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the release request for \`${tag}\` gave no HTTP status." ;;
300	    *) could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the release request for \`${tag}\` returned HTTP ${http_status}." ;;
301	  esac
302	
303	  if [[ -z "${missing}" ]]; then
304	    continue
305	  fi
306	  gap_count=$((gap_count + 1))
307	
308	  {
309	    what=""
310	    for item in ${missing}; do
311	      case "${item}" in
312	        tag) what="${what:+${what}, }tag \`${tag}\` is missing" ;;
313	        release) what="${what:+${what}, }GitHub release \`${tag}\` is missing" ;;
314	        draft-release) what="${what:+${what}, }GitHub release \`${tag}\` is a draft" ;;
315	      esac
316	    done
317	    echo "#### \`${name}\` ${version}: ${what}"
318	    echo
319	    case " ${missing} " in
320	      *" tag "*)
321	        echo "Make the tag. release-plz makes the tag object before the ref, so first"
322	        echo "look for the tag object SHA in the log of the failed run. If you find one,"
323	        echo "check it. The tag name and the object SHA must match the release commit."
324	        echo
325	        echo '```bash'
326	        echo "gh api repos/${repo}/git/tags/<tag-object-sha> --jq '{tag, sha: .object.sha}'"
327	        echo '```'
328	        echo
329	        echo "If the tag object exists, skip the first command below. Else make a new"
330	        echo "annotated tag object. \`${sha}\` is the commit of this run. It is correct"
331	        echo "only if this run published ${name} ${version}. The gap can come from an"
332	        echo "earlier run. In that case, use the commit that bumped the version."
333	        echo
334	        echo '```bash'
335	        echo "gh api -X POST repos/${repo}/git/tags -f tag=${tag} -f message=${tag} -f object=${sha} -f type=commit --jq .sha"
336	        echo "gh api -X POST repos/${repo}/git/refs -f ref=refs/tags/${tag} -f sha=<tag-object-sha>"
337	        echo '```'
338	        echo
339	        ;;
340	    esac
341	    case " ${missing} " in
342	      *" draft-release "*)
343	        echo "Publish the draft release, or delete it and make it again with the command"
344	        echo "below."
345	        echo
346	        ;;
347	    esac
348	    case " ${missing} " in
349	      *" release "*|*" draft-release "*)
350	        echo "Make the release. Use the ${version} section of \`${dir}/CHANGELOG.md\` as"
351	        echo "the notes file. The tag must exist first. GitHub returns 404 for a draft"
352	        echo "release, so first look for a draft with this tag. \`gh release list\` shows"
353	        echo "only 30 releases, so use the API with pagination:"
354	        echo
355	        echo '```bash'
356	        echo "gh api --paginate \"repos/${repo}/releases?per_page=100\" --jq '.[] | select(.tag_name == \"${tag}\" and .draft == true) | .id'"
357	        echo '```'
358	        echo
359	        echo "If there is one, publish it with \`gh release edit ${tag} --draft=false --latest=false\`."
360	        echo "Do not make a second release."
361	        echo
362	        echo '```bash'
363	        echo "gh release create ${tag} --verify-tag --latest=false --title ${tag} --notes-file <file with the ${version} section of ${dir}/CHANGELOG.md>"
364	        echo '```'
365	        echo
366	        ;;
367	    esac
368	  } >> "${gaps}"
369	done 3< "${packages}"
370	
371	finish

115	# Temporal Rust SDK (Public Preview; crates.io since 2026-02-19). TLS risk (requires
116	# verification on every temporalio-* bump): temporalio-common CAN pull a second
117	# reqwest + TLS stack via opentelemetry-otlp, but only behind its `otel` feature —
118	# both `opentelemetry-otlp` and `reqwest` are `optional = true` there, and
119	# `tls-aws-lc` names opentelemetry-otlp only *weakly* (`opentelemetry-otlp?/…`), so
120	# it does not activate it. Nothing in this workspace enables `otel`, and the lock
121	# carries exactly one reqwest. The standing risk this comment guards is therefore a
122	# FUTURE feature flip enabling `otel`, not a present-day second stack. (Corrected in
123	# SMA-622: the previous wording claimed an *unconditional* pull of reqwest 0.12 via
124	# hyper-rustls. That was never true — not at 0.7.0 either — and re-verifying against
125	# a fiction is worse than having no comment.)
126	# Safety still rests on all consumers unifying on the single shared rustls 0.23
127	# instance, which resolves to aws-lc-rs for every consumer — verify with
128	# `cargo tree -i ring --all-features -e normal --target all`, which must print
129	# "nothing to print". Use `--target all`: cargo otherwise resolves for the host only,
130	# and temporalio-client 1.0.0 carries a non-optional tokio-rustls plus an optional
131	# rustls-native-certs — exactly the deps most likely to be platform-gated.
132	# The `-e normal` is load-bearing: plain `cargo tree -i ring` DOES report a hit via
133	# `rcgen`, a dev-dependency of paigasus-helikon-tools that has nothing to do with the
134	# TLS stack. Only a *normal* dependency on ring would mean a second CryptoProvider.
135	# The `ephemeral-server` feature (temporalio-sdk-core) additionally pulls its own
136	# reqwest+TLS stack and must stay unenabled; runtime-temporal's integration tests use
137	# the external-server env gate instead.

139	# temporalio_sdk_core crates/` is empty); it exists solely to force `tls-aws-lc`

148	# `build-no-default-features`, and `PROTOC` set to a path that does not exist.

Internal, unpublished (`publish = false`) crate housing the shared `Session`

writers). Consumed as a path-only dev-dependency by the session backend crates.

1	# Crate overview
2	
3	The workspace is **21 crates** under `crates/`, all named `paigasus-helikon-*` (plus the `paigasus-helikon` facade itself), plus three further internal, non-published Cargo workspace members outside `crates/` (see below). This page is the ownership map: one row per crate, what it owns, whether it is published, and how the crates depend on each other.
4	
5	For orientation — how to pick crates and add them to your `Cargo.toml` — see [workspace layout](../getting-started/workspace-layout.md). For the rendered rustdoc, see [API docs](./api-docs.md).
6	
7	## Dependency direction
8	
9	- `paigasus-helikon-core` is the root: it owns the trait surface, the agent loop, the event stream, and the carrier types. It depends on no other workspace crate.
10	- The provider, session, tool, MCP, and runtime crates each depend on `core` and on nothing else in the workspace (`-tools` carries a path-only dev-dep on `-providers-openai` for an example; it is stripped from the published manifest).
11	- `paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate; its `#[tool]` expansion targets `core` types in the consumer's crate.
12	- `paigasus-helikon` is the **facade**: it re-exports `core` unconditionally and the sibling crates behind Cargo features. Application crates normally depend on the facade alone and turn on the features they need.
13	- `paigasus-helikon-cli` consumes `core` and the sibling crates it needs (`-evals`, `-runtime-tokio`, `-providers-openai`, `-providers-anthropic`, `-mcp`) directly — not the facade. It publishes to crates.io as a binary crate; its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out) and carries no stability guarantee, publishing only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves.
14

The internal `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` row is the one exception — it is `publish = false`, so it has no docs.rs page and no version to report. Versions move every release, so any number mirrored here would be wrong within days.

190	#### Components reserved but not yet emitting
191	
192	The component name is derived mechanically from the crate name: strip the
193	`paigasus-helikon-` prefix, then a leading `providers-` if present, then
194	replace remaining `-` with `_`. The facade crate, `paigasus-helikon`, is the
195	one exception to the rule itself rather than to its output: stripping the
196	`paigasus-helikon-` prefix leaves nothing to work with (there is no trailing
197	`-<name>`), so its component is `facade` by fiat, not by the derivation.
198	
199	Nine crates have a name under this rule (eight derived, plus the facade's
200	`facade`) with no call site emitting on it yet, because those crates carry no
201	`tracing` instrumentation today: `facade`, `macros`, `mcp`, `evals`,
202	`cli`, `sessions_sqlite`, `sessions_postgres`, `sessions_redis`,
203	`sessions_testkit`. They are not in the table above — a row for a component
204	nothing emits would fail the guard that checks the table against source — but
205	the names are reserved: when one of those crates starts emitting, it uses the
206	derived (or, for the facade, the by-fiat) name, and no other component may
207	claim it in the meantime (see the no-prefix-collision rule below).

351	Releases are automated by [release-plz](https://release-plz.dev). The contract:
352

354	   [Conventional Commits](#conventional-commits) section above for the
355	   type → semver mapping; `<scope>` is informational at release time
356	   (release-plz attributes by files changed, not by scope).
357	
358	2. **A rolling release PR.** The `release-plz` workflow runs on every push to
359	   `main` and maintains one open release PR titled `chore: release v...`. It
360	   enumerates which crates will bump and to what version, and shows the
361	   generated `CHANGELOG.md` additions. Reviewers verify, then squash-merge.
362	
363	3. **Merging the release PR** triggers the workflow's `release-plz-release`
364	   job, which creates per-crate git tags (`<crate>-v<version>`), GitHub

370	   release PR's `Cargo.toml` / `CHANGELOG.md` directly — release-plz
371	   respects manual edits and won't clobber them on subsequent runs.

373	5. **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure.** Any commit that edits

1	# Workspace layout
2	
3	Paigasus Helikon is a Cargo workspace of **21 crates** under `crates/`, all in the
4	`paigasus-helikon-*` namespace. As a consumer you rarely depend on more than two of them directly: the
5	`paigasus-helikon-core` trait crate, or — more commonly — the `paigasus-helikon` **facade**,
6	which re-exports `core` plus the optional sibling crates behind Cargo features.
7	
8	This page is about **how to depend** on the SDK. For the per-crate ownership table,
9	see [Crates reference](../reference/crates.md).
10	
11	## The facade
12	
13	`paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` **unconditionally** as
14	`paigasus_helikon::core`, and each optional sibling crate behind a kebab-case feature. With no
15	features you still get the full core surface: the traits (`Agent`, `Model`, `Tool`, `Session`)
16	plus the carrier and impl types (`LlmAgent`, `RunContext`, the event stream). Features add the
17	concrete adapters and runtimes on top.
18	
19	Feature names are kebab-case in `Cargo.toml`; the re-export module aliases are snake-case.
20	
21	| Feature | Re-exported as | Surface |
22	| --- | --- | --- |
23	| *(always on)* | `paigasus_helikon::core` | `paigasus-helikon-core` — traits, agent loop, event stream, carrier types |
24	| `macros` | `paigasus_helikon::macros`, plus `paigasus_helikon::tool` and `paigasus_helikon::tools` | `#[tool]` attribute + `tools!` macro |
25	| `openai` *(alias `providers-openai`)* | `paigasus_helikon::openai` *(also `providers_openai`)* | `OpenAiModel` adapter |
26	| `anthropic` | `paigasus_helikon::anthropic` | `AnthropicModel` adapter |
27	| `litellm` | `paigasus_helikon::litellm` | `LiteLlmModel` adapter — LiteLLM proxy (OpenAI-compatible gateway) |
28	| `mcp` | `paigasus_helikon::mcp` | rmcp-based MCP client/server |
29	| `tools` | `paigasus_helikon::tools` | sandboxed Read/Write/Edit/Bash tools |

# Workspace layout

Paigasus Helikon is a Cargo workspace of **21 crates** under `crates/`, all in the
`paigasus-helikon-*` namespace. As a consumer you rarely depend on more than two of them directly: the
`paigasus-helikon-core` trait crate, or — more commonly — the `paigasus-helikon` **facade**,
which re-exports `core` plus the optional sibling crates behind Cargo features.

This page is about **how to depend** on the SDK. For the per-crate ownership table,
see [Crates reference](../reference/crates.md).

## The facade

`paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` **unconditionally** as
`paigasus_helikon::core`, and each optional sibling crate behind a kebab-case feature. With no
features you still get the full core surface: the traits (`Agent`, `Model`, `Tool`, `Session`)
plus the carrier and impl types (`LlmAgent`, `RunContext`, the event stream). Features add the
concrete adapters and runtimes on top.

Feature names are kebab-case in `Cargo.toml`; the re-export module aliases are snake-case.

| Feature | Re-exported as | Surface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *(always on)* | `paigasus_helikon::core` | `paigasus-helikon-core` — traits, agent loop, event stream, carrier types |
| `macros` | `paigasus_helikon::macros`, plus `paigasus_helikon::tool` and `paigasus_helikon::tools` | `#[tool]` attribute + `tools!` macro |
| `openai` *(alias `providers-openai`)* | `paigasus_helikon::openai` *(also `providers_openai`)* | `OpenAiModel` adapter |
| `anthropic` | `paigasus_helikon::anthropic` | `AnthropicModel` adapter |
| `litellm` | `paigasus_helikon::litellm` | `LiteLlmModel` adapter — LiteLLM proxy (OpenAI-compatible gateway) |
| `mcp` | `paigasus_helikon::mcp` | rmcp-based MCP client/server |
| `tools` | `paigasus_helikon::tools` | sandboxed Read/Write/Edit/Bash tools |
| `tools-web` | *(extends `tools`)* | adds the WebFetch / WebSearch network tools |
| `runtime-tokio` | `paigasus_helikon::runtime_tokio` | ephemeral Tokio runner |
| `runtime-axum` | `paigasus_helikon::runtime_axum` | self-hosted HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server — see [Axum Server Runtime](../concepts/axum-server.md) |
| `runtime-temporal` | `paigasus_helikon::runtime_temporal` | durable Temporal-backed runner — see [Runtimes](../concepts/runtimes.md) |
| `runtime-agentcore` | `paigasus_helikon::runtime_agentcore` | AWS Bedrock AgentCore container shim — see [Runtimes](../concepts/runtimes.md) |
| `sessions-sqlite` | `paigasus_helikon::sessions_sqlite` | SQLite `Session` backend |
| `evals` | `paigasus_helikon::evals` | evaluation harness — datasets, evaluators, `MockModel`, SQLite/Parquet trace sinks |

In addition, `paigasus_helikon::schema::strict` re-exports the JSON-Schema strict-mode normalizer
from `core`, regardless of features.

### `tools` name clash

`paigasus_helikon::tools` resolves to **two different items** when both `macros` and `tools` are
enabled: the `tools!` function-like macro (from `macros`) and the sandboxed-tools **module**
(from the `tools` crate). They live in separate namespaces, so Rust disambiguates by use site — a
macro invocation `tools![...]` versus a path `tools::SomeTool`. Be explicit about which you mean.

## Published vs stub crates

Twenty crates carry real implementations and are published on crates.io / docs.rs:

- `paigasus-helikon-core` — the dependency root (traits, agent loop, carrier types)
- `paigasus-helikon` — the facade
- `paigasus-helikon-macros` — `#[tool]` + `tools!`
- `paigasus-helikon-providers-openai`
- `paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic`
- `paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock`
- `paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini`
- `paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm`
- `paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite`
- `paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres`
- `paigasus-helikon-sessions-redis`
- `paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio`
- `paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum` — self-hosted HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server (see [Axum Server Runtime](../concepts/axum-server.md))
- `paigasus-helikon-runtime-actix` — self-hosted actix-web HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server (same public surface as `runtime-axum`)
- `paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal` — durable Temporal-backed runner (see [Runtimes](../concepts/runtimes.md))
- `paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore` — AWS Bedrock AgentCore container shim (see [Runtimes](../concepts/runtimes.md))
- `paigasus-helikon-mcp`
- `paigasus-helikon-tools`
- `paigasus-helikon-evals` — evaluation harness: datasets, evaluators, `MockModel`, SQLite/Parquet trace sinks
- `paigasus-helikon-cli` — published binary crate (`helikon` / `paigasus-helikon` binaries); its lib target is internal and carries no stability guarantee, publishing only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves

Zero name-claim stubs remain in the workspace. The one crate that rounds out the
workspace's 21 without publishing is `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit`, an internal
`Session` conformance test harness (`publish = false` by design).

## Picking your surface

**Depend on `core` alone** when you only need the trait definitions — for example a crate that
implements its own `Model` or `Tool<Ctx>` and doesn't pull in any provider:

```bash
cargo add paigasus-helikon-core
```

**Depend on the facade** for everything else, selecting only the features you use. A typical
single-agent app with OpenAI, the tool macros, and SQLite-backed sessions:

```bash
cargo add paigasus-helikon --features openai,macros,sessions-sqlite
cargo add tokio@1 --features macros,rt-multi-thread
cargo add serde@1 --features derive
cargo add anyhow@1 schemars@1 serde_json@1
```

That pulls `paigasus-helikon-providers-openai`, `paigasus-helikon-macros`, and
`paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite` transitively; everything else stays out of your dependency
graph. Imports then come from the facade's re-export modules:

```rust
use paigasus_helikon::core::{Agent, AgentInput, LlmAgent, MemorySession, RunContext};
use paigasus_helikon::openai::OpenAiModel;
use paigasus_helikon::{tool, tools};
```

Swap providers by swapping one feature and one import: `anthropic` /
`paigasus_helikon::anthropic::AnthropicModel` instead of `openai` / `OpenAiModel`. Add `tools`
(or `tools-web`) for the sandboxed file/shell tools, `mcp` for MCP servers, and `runtime-tokio`
for the runner boundary.

## Next steps

- [Quickstart](./quickstart.md) — a complete first agent.
- [Core primitives](../concepts/core-primitives.md) — the seven traits `core` defines.
- [Model providers](../concepts/model-providers.md) — `OpenAiModel` and `AnthropicModel`.
- [Crates reference](../reference/crates.md) — per-crate ownership and dependency direction.

1	# Introduction
2	
3	`paigasus-helikon` is a Rust SDK for building agentic AI systems. It separates slow-moving primitives (types, traits, message protocols) from fast-moving parts (provider SDKs, execution runtimes, tool catalogs), so downstream projects can pick the surface they need without dragging in the rest.
4	
5	The SDK does not pick a deployment story, a hosting story, or an observability stack for you. Bring your own.
6	
7	## What's here
8	
9	The single-facade crate `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and pulls in sibling crates behind kebab-case Cargo features. The shipped surface covers an end-to-end single-agent loop plus the first multi-agent pieces:
10	
11	- **Agent loop.** `LlmAgent::builder` assembles an `Agent`; `agent.run(ctx, input)` returns an event stream you collect with `RunResultStreaming`. Core carrier types (`RunContext`, `AgentInput`, `HookRegistry`, `MemorySession`, `CancellationToken`, `TracerHandle`) live in `paigasus_helikon::core`.
12	- **Providers.** `paigasus_helikon::openai::OpenAiModel` (feature `openai`) and `paigasus_helikon::anthropic::AnthropicModel` (feature `anthropic`). Switching providers is a one-line `Model` swap on the builder.
13	- **Tools.** The `#[tool]` attribute and `tools!` macro (feature `macros`) turn an `async fn` into a registered, JSON-Schema-typed tool. The `tools` feature adds sandboxed Read/Write/Edit/Bash tools; `tools-web` adds the `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` network tools.
14	- **Sessions.** `MemorySession` ships in `core`; `paigasus_helikon::sessions_sqlite` (feature `sessions-sqlite`) is a persistent SQLite `Session` backend.
15	- **Runtime.** `paigasus_helikon::runtime_tokio` (feature `runtime-tokio`) is the default ephemeral Tokio runner. `paigasus_helikon::runtime_axum` (feature `runtime-axum`) is the self-hosted HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server built on axum — see [Axum Server Runtime](concepts/axum-server.md). `paigasus_helikon::runtime_actix` (feature `runtime-actix`) is the same self-hosted HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server built on actix-web instead of axum. `paigasus_helikon::runtime_temporal` (feature `runtime-temporal`) is a durable runner backed by the Temporal Rust SDK, and `paigasus_helikon::runtime_agentcore` (feature `runtime-agentcore`) is an AWS Bedrock AgentCore container shim — see [Runtimes](concepts/runtimes.md) for both.
16	- **Multi-agent and MCP.** `Handoff::to(..)` wires triage-style delegation between agents; `paigasus_helikon::mcp` (feature `mcp`) is an rmcp-based MCP client/server wrapper. Guardrails, hooks, and permissions hang off the `HookRegistry` carried in every `RunContext`.
17	- **Evals.** `paigasus_helikon::evals` (feature `evals`) is an evaluation harness: JSONL datasets, an `Evaluator` trait with four built-ins, a `MockModel` for deterministic replay, and SQLite/Parquet trace sinks — see [Observability & Evaluation](concepts/observability-evaluation.md).
18	
19	Twenty crates are published to [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/paigasus-helikon) with rustdoc on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon).
20	
21	A minimal run:
22	
23	```rust
24	use paigasus_helikon::core::{
25	    Agent, AgentInput, LlmAgent, RunContext, RunResultStreaming,
26	};
27	use paigasus_helikon::openai::OpenAiModel;
28	
29	#[tokio::main]
30	async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31	    let model = OpenAiModel::chat("gpt-5-mini").build()?;
32	
33	    let agent = LlmAgent::builder::<()>()
34	        .name("budget-assistant")
35	        .model(model)
36	        .instructions("You are a budgeting assistant. ...")
37	        .build();
38	
39	    let ctx: RunContext<()> = RunContext::ephemeral(());
40	
41	    let input = AgentInput::from_user_text("How am I doing on my dining budget this month?");
42	
43	    let stream = agent.run(ctx, input).await?;
44	    let result = RunResultStreaming::new(stream).collect().await?;
45	
46	    println!("{}", result.final_output);
47	    Ok(())
48	}
49	```
50	
51	Start at [Quickstart](getting-started/quickstart.md), then read [Core primitives](concepts/core-primitives.md) for the trait surface.
52	
53	Tracked work lives in Linear under the project **Paigasus Helikon** (issues are prefixed `SMA-`).

323	system messages: Anthropic hoists them to the top-level `system` field; OpenAI
324	concatenates them at the top of the conversation. The summary reaches the model
325	as a top-level instruction, not as a positional cutover in the message stream.
326	
327	**Concurrency.** `CompactingSession` assumes a **single logical writer per
328	session** — the normal runner model where one run owns the session and appends
329	serially. The inner backend remains fully durable and concurrency-safe; the
330	compaction bookkeeping is not atomic against a concurrent append through the
331	same wrapper. Concurrent writers should share the same *inner* backend directly,
332	not a single wrapper instance.

338	
339	| Test | What it verifies |
340	| --- | --- |
341	| `run_append_read` | Events written by `append` are returned by `events` in order |
342	| `run_watermark_exclusive` | `events(Some(SequenceId(n)))` returns only positions strictly after `n` |
343	| `run_projection` | `snapshot()` equals `project(&events(None))` |
344	| `run_concurrent_writers` | 16 concurrent tasks × 10 appends each — every event present exactly once |

347	backends all run `run_all`. Adding a new backend means passing this suite before

10	
11	- **Agent loop.** `LlmAgent::builder` assembles an `Agent`; `agent.run(ctx, input)` returns an event stream you collect with `RunResultStreaming`. Core carrier types (`RunContext`, `AgentInput`, `HookRegistry`, `MemorySession`, `CancellationToken`, `TracerHandle`) live in `paigasus_helikon::core`.
12	- **Providers.** `paigasus_helikon::openai::OpenAiModel` (feature `openai`) and `paigasus_helikon::anthropic::AnthropicModel` (feature `anthropic`). Switching providers is a one-line `Model` swap on the builder.
13	- **Tools.** The `#[tool]` attribute and `tools!` macro (feature `macros`) turn an `async fn` into a registered, JSON-Schema-typed tool. The `tools` feature adds sandboxed Read/Write/Edit/Bash tools; `tools-web` adds the `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` network tools.
14	- **Sessions.** `MemorySession` ships in `core`; `paigasus_helikon::sessions_sqlite` (feature `sessions-sqlite`) is a persistent SQLite `Session` backend.
15	- **Runtime.** `paigasus_helikon::runtime_tokio` (feature `runtime-tokio`) is the default ephemeral Tokio runner. `paigasus_helikon::runtime_axum` (feature `runtime-axum`) is the self-hosted HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server built on axum — see [Axum Server Runtime](concepts/axum-server.md). `paigasus_helikon::runtime_actix` (feature `runtime-actix`) is the same self-hosted HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server built on actix-web instead of axum. `paigasus_helikon::runtime_temporal` (feature `runtime-temporal`) is a durable runner backed by the Temporal Rust SDK, and `paigasus_helikon::runtime_agentcore` (feature `runtime-agentcore`) is an AWS Bedrock AgentCore container shim — see [Runtimes](concepts/runtimes.md) for both.

# paigasus-helikon

Paigasus AI SDK — codename **Helikon**. A Rust SDK for building AI agents with pluggable providers, runtimes, and tools.

[![CI](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/paigasus-helikon.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/paigasus-helikon)
[![docs.rs](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon)

## What it is

`paigasus-helikon` is a Rust SDK for building agentic AI systems. It separates the slow-moving primitives (types, traits, message protocols) from the fast-moving parts (provider SDKs, execution runtimes, tool catalogs), so downstream projects can pick the surface they need without dragging in the rest.

The SDK does not pick a deployment story, a hosting story, or an observability stack for you. Bring your own.

## The codename

In Greek myth, Mount Helicon (Greek: Ἑλικῶν, *Helikōn*) is the home of the Muses. When Pegasus struck the mountainside with his hoof, the **Hippocrene** spring burst forth — the literal source of poetic inspiration that the Muses drew from.

Paigasus is the umbrella; Helikon is the spring. The SDK is the artifact you draw from when building agents on top.

## Install

```bash
cargo add paigasus-helikon --features openai,macros
```

Turn on the features you need — `openai`, `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `gemini`, `litellm`, `mcp`, `tools`, `tools-web`, `tools-os-sandbox`, `tools-microvm`, `sessions-sqlite`, `sessions-postgres`, `sessions-redis`, `runtime-tokio`, `runtime-axum`, `runtime-actix`, `runtime-temporal`, `runtime-agentcore`, `evals`, `macros`. See the [crate roster](https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/reference/crates.html) for the full feature → crate map, and [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon) for the current published version.

## Workspace at a glance

Twenty-one crates under `crates/`. Twenty are published to crates.io; one is an internal test harness (`publish = false`); one of the published crates (the CLI) is binary-only, publishing a lib target with no stability guarantees purely so `cargo install` resolves.

- **`paigasus-helikon`** — facade re-exporting `core` plus opt-in sibling crates by feature flag.
- **`paigasus-helikon-core`** — type system, traits, the agent loop, runtime-agnostic primitives.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros`** — the `#[tool]` attribute and `tools!` proc macros.
- **`paigasus-helikon-providers-openai`**, **`-anthropic`**, **`-bedrock`**, **`-gemini`**, **`-litellm`** — LLM provider adapters.
- **`paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite`** — SQLite-backed session persistence.
- **`paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres`** — PostgreSQL-backed session persistence (JSONB event log, advisory-lock concurrency, aws-lc-rs TLS).
- **`paigasus-helikon-sessions-redis`** — Redis Streams-backed session persistence (atomic Lua append, BYO-`ConnectionManager` for TLS).
- **`paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio`** — the default ephemeral Tokio runner.
- **`paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum`** — self-hosted HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server (`AgentServer` builder, 6 endpoints: one-shot JSON, SSE streaming, async detached, WebSocket event replay, agent list, OpenAPI schema; replayable runs with TTL+count retention).
- **`paigasus-helikon-runtime-actix`** — API-identical actix-web port of `runtime-axum`, for embedding into an existing actix-web service; same routes and wire format. The differences are the mount seam (`configure()` vs `router()`), listener type, entrypoint attribute, one-shot client-disconnect semantics, and the request type its extension traits take (`AuthLayer`/`ContextProvider` receive an `actix_web::HttpRequest` rather than axum request parts).
- **`paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal`** — durable runner over the official Temporal Rust SDK (`TemporalRunner`; per-model-turn and per-tool-call activities; a run that crashes mid-tool-call resumes from the last completed activity).
- **`paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore`** — AWS Bedrock AgentCore container shim (`AgentCoreServer`; all four container protocols — HTTP on 8080 with an optional WebSocket, MCP on 8000, A2A on 9000, AG-UI on 8080; ships a multi-stage Dockerfile and CDK deployment snippet).
- **`paigasus-helikon-tools`** — sandboxed Read/Write/Edit/Bash tools (+ `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` behind `web`; OS-enforced containment behind `os-sandbox`; microVM containment via forkd/Firecracker behind `microvm`, experimental — SMA-437: includes `EgressProxy`, `EgressPolicy`, and `Isolation::Proxied` for domain-filtered egress enforcement).
- **`paigasus-helikon-mcp`** — Model Context Protocol client and server integration.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli`** — published binary crate: `helikon` and `paigasus-helikon` binaries (`cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli`) with `repl`, `eval run`, and `mcp serve` subcommands driven by an `agents.toml` sidecar; its lib target publishes only so `cargo install` works, and carries no stability guarantee.
- **`paigasus-helikon-evals`** — evaluation harness: JSONL datasets, an `Evaluator` trait with four built-ins (`ExactMatch`, `JsonSchemaConformance`, `LlmJudge`, `ToolUseTrajectory`), a `MockModel` for deterministic replay, and SQLite/Parquet trace sinks.

See the [crate roster](https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/reference/crates.html) for each crate's concern and published state; each published crate's row links to its docs.rs page for the current version.

## Documentation

The public documentation site is published at <https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/> — a guided mdBook covering the [quickstart](https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/getting-started/quickstart.html), the core concepts, and the [crate roster](https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/reference/crates.html).

To build it locally: `cd docs/book && mdbook serve` (requires `mdbook` and `mdbook-linkcheck` installed via `cargo install`; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md#documentation-site) for exact versions).

The architectural source-of-truth currently lives in Notion (internal): ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). External readers should treat the Notion link as an artifact pointer rather than a destination — content migrates into the published book as the SDK lands.

Tracked work lives in Linear under the project **Paigasus Helikon** (issues are prefixed `SMA-`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for branching, testing, and release workflows. By participating you agree to the [Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). For security disclosures see [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md).

180	  - `TemporalAgentWorkerBuilder::with_seeded_ctx` / `::try_with_seeded_ctx` — seeded `Ctx` factories that reconstitute the per-run context from a client-supplied `serde_json::Value` seed; `try_with_seeded_ctx` maps a rejected seed to a **non-retryable** activity failure (fail-fast on a malformed/hostile seed) rather than a silent default identity
181	  - `runner::TemporalRunnerConfig::with_ctx_seed` — attaches the request-scoped seed on the client side; threaded through `payloads::WorkflowInput::ctx_seed` (new, `#[serde(default)]`, public field)
182	  - `TemporalAgentWorkerBuilder::heartbeat_interval` — opt-in liveness heartbeats on the `call_model`/`invoke_tool` activities (floored to 1s; sets `heartbeat_timeout = 2 × interval` on those two activities only), speeding up crash reclamation; off by default
183	  - No new re-exports — build a `WorkerPosture` by importing `PermissionMode` / `DenyRule` / `AllowRule` / `GuardRule` / `PermissionPolicy` / `ApprovalHandler` from `paigasus-helikon-core` directly
184	
185	### Upgrade notes
186	
187	- The wire additions above are **additive by construction**: `WorkflowInput::ctx_seed` is `#[serde(default)]`, so a payload serialized by a pre-SMA-455 worker still deserializes; the changed `render_instructions`/`invoke_tool` activity-input shape only affects **newly-scheduled** activities (an already-completed activity replays its recorded result from history, it does not re-execute). This is a reasoned claim, not a guarantee proven against every upgrade path — **drain-before-upgrade / blue-green task queues remain the conservative, recommended path** for any worker-version bump, same as before this release.
188	- Manually validated via the crate's unit test suite (seed round-trip, default-equivalence, fail-fast-on-bad-seed, heartbeat wiring); no automated live-Temporal determinism/replay check for the new activity-input shape ships in this release.

198	### Added
199	
200	- *(runtime-temporal)* SMA-332 initial real implementation: Temporal-backed durable `Runner`
201	  - `TemporalRunner` implementing `paigasus-helikon-core`'s `Runner` trait — agent runs execute as a deterministic Temporal workflow, replayed from history on resumption, resuming from the last completed activity after a worker crash
202	  - `TemporalAgentWorker` builder — registers `LlmAgent`s onto a task queue, serving the agent-loop workflow and its activities
203	  - Pure durable loop driver decoupling agent-loop decisions from Temporal's workflow-context APIs, enabling deterministic replay
204	  - Per-activity timeout overrides on the worker builder
205	  - Registration fails fast (`RegistrationError`) on hooks, guardrails, and handoffs — not supported by the v0 constraint set; nested agent-as-tool is permitted but runs non-durably inside its tool activity
206	  - Worker-side posture: the worker fabricates its own `RunContext` rather than accepting one from the client, and applies fixed safe defaults (redaction on, destructive-effect guards on); worker-side posture configuration is future work
207	  - Env-gated live integration suite (`TEMPORAL_TEST_SERVER`) covering crash-resume, cancellation with partial transcripts, session persistence, and model error handling

name: pr-title

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize]

concurrency:
  # pull_request_target sets github.ref to the base branch (refs/heads/main),
  # so keying on github.ref would cause two open PRs to cancel each other.
  # Key on the PR number instead — cancel-in-progress then only kills stale
  # runs for the *same* PR.
  group: pr-title-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  pull-requests: read
  statuses: write

jobs:
  pr-title:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Pinned to SHA; Dependabot's gh-actions group keeps this updated.
      - uses: amannn/action-semantic-pull-request@2252a14e810aa9b85c2d560bd7070c802206ecf6 # v6.1.2
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          # keep-in-sync-with: .versionrc types
          types: |
            feat
            fix
            build
            chore
            ci
            docs
            style
            refactor
            perf
            test
            revert
          # keep-in-sync-with: .versionrc scopeRegex
          scopes: |
            core
            cli
            facade
            macros
            mcp
            tools
            evals
            providers
            providers-openai
            providers-anthropic
            runtime
            runtime-tokio
            runtime-axum
            runtime-temporal
            runtime-agentcore
            runtime-actix
            sessions
            sessions-sqlite
            workspace
            workflows
            ci
            deps
            release
            repo
            docs
            contributing
            readme
            claude
            spec
            specs
            plan
            lints
          requireScope: false
          # Dependabot's auto-generated titles ("chore(deps): Bump …") start the
          # subject with a capital `B` and Dependabot offers no way to lowercase
          # it, so they always trip `subjectPattern`. Exempt its PRs — labeled
          # `area:deps` per .github/dependabot.yml — from validation. With an
          # ignore label the action *passes* (green check), unlike skipping the
          # job, which would leave the required `pr-title` context unreported and
          # block the PR. Human PRs are unaffected.
          ignoreLabels: |
            area:deps
          subjectPattern: '^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$'
          subjectPatternError: |
            PR title subject must not start with an uppercase letter.
            Use sentence case after the colon, e.g. `feat(core): add Model trait`.
            An optional `SMA-### ` prefix is accepted, e.g. `feat(core): SMA-304 add Model trait`.

33	/// Crate directory name (under `crates/`) to its registered
34	/// `paigasus::<component>`, for all 21 workspace members.
35	///
36	/// Ten of the twenty-one are reserved: they are name-claim stubs that emit no
37	/// tracing today, and per the design they must **not** appear in the
38	/// mdBook's component table (`tracing_target_docs.rs` asserts book and
39	/// source agree, and a row for an absent component fails it). They are still
40	/// listed here so a file that later appears under one of them resolves
41	/// instead of silently falling through the lookup, and so the
42	/// directory-existence assertion below covers all 21, not just the eleven
43	/// that are live.
44	///
45	/// Derivation rule for a future crate: strip `paigasus-helikon-`, then strip
46	/// a leading `providers-`, then replace `-` with `_`. The providers' bare
47	/// form (`openai`, not `providers_openai`) is a historical exception,
48	/// preserved because those names are the user-facing vendor names.
49	const CRATE_COMPONENTS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
50	    ("paigasus-helikon", "facade"),
51	    ("paigasus-helikon-cli", "cli"),
52	    ("paigasus-helikon-core", "core"),
53	    ("paigasus-helikon-evals", "evals"),
54	    ("paigasus-helikon-macros", "macros"),
55	    ("paigasus-helikon-mcp", "mcp"),
56	    ("paigasus-helikon-providers-openai", "openai"),
57	    ("paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic", "anthropic"),

59	    ("paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini", "gemini"),

65	    ("paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal", "runtime_temporal"),
66	    ("paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite", "sessions_sqlite"),
67	    ("paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres", "sessions_postgres"),
68	    ("paigasus-helikon-sessions-redis", "sessions_redis"),

73	/// Repo root, derived from this crate's manifest directory rather than the
74	/// process CWD so it survives the member being moved.
75	fn repo_root() -> PathBuf {
76	    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
77	        .join("..")
78	        .join("..")
79	        .canonicalize()
80	        .expect("repo root must resolve from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")
81	}

83	/// Collect `.rs` files under `dir`, skipping build output.
84	///
85	/// Uses [`std::fs::symlink_metadata`] rather than [`Path::is_dir`]: `is_dir`
86	/// follows symlinks, so a symlink pointing at an ancestor directory would
87	/// recurse this walk unboundedly.
88	fn collect_rs(dir: &Path, out: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
89	    let entries = std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read_dir {dir:?}: {e}"));
90	    for entry in entries {
91	        let path = entry.expect("dir entry").path();
92	        let meta = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&path)
93	            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("symlink_metadata {path:?}: {e}"));
94	        if meta.is_symlink() {
95	            continue;
96	        }
97	        let name = path
98	            .file_name()
99	            .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
100	            .unwrap_or_default();
101	        if meta.is_dir() {
102	            if name == "target" || name == ".git" {
103	                continue;
104	            }
105	            collect_rs(&path, out);
106	        } else if name.ends_with(".rs") {
107	            out.push(path);
108	        }
109	    }

# API docs

Per-item Rust API documentation is published on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs). This book covers concepts and worked examples; docs.rs is the source of truth for every type, trait, method, and feature flag. For a higher-level map of which crate owns which concern, see [Crate overview](./crates.md).

## Published crates

- [`paigasus-helikon`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon) — the facade; re-exports `core` and the feature-gated siblings.
- [`paigasus-helikon-core`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-core) — trait surface, agent loop, event stream, carrier types (the dependency root).
- [`paigasus-helikon-macros`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-macros) — the `#[tool]` attribute and `tools!` proc macros.
- [`paigasus-helikon-providers-openai`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai) — OpenAI model adapter.
- [`paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic) — Anthropic model adapter.
- [`paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock) — Amazon Bedrock Converse API model adapter (`BedrockModel`). See [Model providers](../concepts/model-providers.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini) — Google Gemini model adapter (`GeminiModel`; Developer API and Vertex AI). See [Model providers](../concepts/model-providers.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm) — LiteLLM proxy adapter (`LiteLlmModel`; OpenAI-compatible gateway). See [Model providers](../concepts/model-providers.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite) — SQLite `Session` backend.
- [`paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres) — PostgreSQL `Session` backend (`PostgresSession`). See [Sessions](../concepts/sessions.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-sessions-redis`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-sessions-redis) — Redis Streams `Session` backend (`RedisSession`). See [Sessions](../concepts/sessions.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio) — ephemeral Tokio runner.
- [`paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum) — self-hosted HTTP/SSE/WebSocket agent server (`AgentServer` builder, 6 endpoints, replayable runs). See [Axum Server Runtime](../concepts/axum-server.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-runtime-actix`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-runtime-actix) — actix-web port of `runtime-axum` with the same routes and wire format, for embedding into an existing actix-web service. See [Runtimes](../concepts/runtimes.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal) — durable Temporal-backed runner (`TemporalRunner`, crash-resume via Temporal history replay). See [Runtimes](../concepts/runtimes.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore) — AWS Bedrock AgentCore container shim (`AgentCoreServer`, HTTP + MCP protocol contract). See [Runtimes](../concepts/runtimes.md).
- [`paigasus-helikon-mcp`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-mcp) — `rmcp`-based MCP client/server wrapper.
- [`paigasus-helikon-tools`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-tools) — sandboxed `Read`/`Write`/`Edit`/`Bash` tools (plus `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` behind the `web` feature).
- [`paigasus-helikon-evals`](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-evals) — evaluation harness: JSONL datasets, the `Evaluator` trait with four built-ins, `MockModel`, and SQLite/Parquet trace sinks. See [Observability & Evaluation](../concepts/observability-evaluation.md).

The binaries are documented in the [CLI reference](./cli.md) rather than docs.rs.

Most users depend only on the `paigasus-helikon` facade and enable the features they need; the facade docs link out to each sibling. Crate versions move every release — each docs.rs link above shows the current published version, and [Crate overview](./crates.md) maps which crate owns which concern.

## Publish status

All 20 non-internal crates now publish to crates.io — the last two stubs (`paigasus-helikon-evals`, `paigasus-helikon-cli`) ascended to real implementations in SMA-332/SMA-333, following `-runtime-axum`, `-runtime-temporal`, and `-runtime-agentcore` before them. The lone exception is `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit`, an internal `Session` conformance test harness that is `publish = false` by design, not a stub awaiting an ascend.

## Building locally

```bash
cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps --open
```

1	//! The [`Session`] trait and its carrier types.
2	//!
3	//! `Session` models conversation persistence as an **append-only event
4	//! log**, not a flat message list. The event-log shape gives evals
5	//! (deterministic replay), durability (Temporal/Restate-style event
6	//! sourcing), and an audit trail for regulated deployments.
7	
8	use async_trait::async_trait;
9	use jiff::Timestamp;
10	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
11	
12	use crate::{AgentEvent, ContentPart, Item};
13	
14	/// Conversation persistence as an append-only event log.
15	///
16	/// See the *Sessions* concept page for the rationale.
17	///
18	/// # Example
19	///
20	/// ```
21	/// use async_trait::async_trait;
22	/// use paigasus_helikon_core::{
23	///     ConversationSnapshot, SequenceId, Session, SessionError, SessionEvent,
24	/// };
25	///
26	/// struct MemorySession;
27	///
28	/// #[async_trait]
29	/// impl Session for MemorySession {
30	///     async fn append(
31	///         &self,
32	///         _events: &[SessionEvent],
33	///     ) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
34	///         Ok(())
35	///     }
36	///
37	///     async fn events(
38	///         &self,
39	///         _since: Option<SequenceId>,
40	///     ) -> Result<Vec<SessionEvent>, SessionError> {
41	///         Ok(Vec::new())
42	///     }
43	///
44	///     async fn snapshot(&self) -> Result<ConversationSnapshot, SessionError> {
45	///         Ok(ConversationSnapshot::default())
46	///     }
47	/// }
48	/// ```
49	#[async_trait]
50	pub trait Session: Send + Sync {
51	    /// Append events to the log.
52	    async fn append(&self, events: &[SessionEvent]) -> Result<(), SessionError>;
53	
54	    /// Read events from the log, optionally only those after `since`.
55	    async fn events(&self, since: Option<SequenceId>) -> Result<Vec<SessionEvent>, SessionError>;
56	
57	    /// Compute (or read) a [`ConversationSnapshot`] projection of the log.
58	    async fn snapshot(&self) -> Result<ConversationSnapshot, SessionError>;
59	}
60	
61	/// One entry in the conversation event log.
62	///
63	/// `UserMessage` / `AssistantMessage` / `ToolReturned` carry
64	/// `Vec<ContentPart>` directly (not `Item`) because the SessionEvent
65	/// variant *is* the role — wrapping `Item::UserMessage` inside
66	/// `SessionEvent::UserMessage` would double-tag.
67	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
68	#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
69	#[non_exhaustive]
70	pub enum SessionEvent {
71	    /// A user-authored message.
72	    ///
73	    /// The enum is marked `#[non_exhaustive]` at the enum level (not per
74	    /// variant) so downstream tests and fixtures can construct variants
75	    /// by struct-init to pin a deterministic `ts`. Don't tighten this to
76	    /// per-variant `#[non_exhaustive]`.
77	    UserMessage {
78	        /// Content blocks of the message.
79	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
80	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
81	        ts: Timestamp,
82	    },
83	    /// An assistant-authored message attributed to a named agent.
84	    AssistantMessage {
85	        /// Content blocks of the message.
86	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
87	        /// Name of the emitting [`crate::Agent`]. `String` (not `Option`)
88	        /// because the runner always knows which agent emitted when
89	        /// appending to the log.
90	        agent: String,
91	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
92	        ts: Timestamp,
93	    },
94	    /// The runner invoked a tool.
95	    ToolCalled {
96	        /// Provider-assigned call identifier.
97	        call_id: String,
98	        /// Tool name.
99	        name: String,
100	        /// JSON arguments.
101	        args: serde_json::Value,
102	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
103	        ts: Timestamp,
104	    },
105	    /// The tool returned.
106	    ToolReturned {
107	        /// Matching call identifier.
108	        call_id: String,
109	        /// Content blocks of the tool's output (Anthropic permits
110	        /// text + image inside a tool result).
111	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
112	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
113	        ts: Timestamp,
114	    },
115	    /// Control transferred from one agent to another.
116	    HandoffOccurred {
117	        /// Outgoing agent name.
118	        from: String,
119	        /// Incoming agent name.
120	        to: String,
121	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
122	        ts: Timestamp,
123	    },
124	    /// Older events were compacted into a summary.
125	    ///
126	    /// **Provider-translator caveat:** [`project`] renders this as
127	    /// [`Item::System`]. Both shipped provider translators reshape
128	    /// `Item::System`: Anthropic hoists every system block into the
129	    /// top-level `system` field, and OpenAI concatenates multiple system
130	    /// blocks into one at the top of the conversation. The "summary
131	    /// replaces turns 1..N at this position" semantic is therefore
132	    /// observation-only in the event log; the model sees the summary text
133	    /// but as a top-level system instruction, not a positional cutover.
134	    Compacted {
135	        /// LLM-produced summary.
136	        summary: String,
137	        /// Number of events the summary replaces. `u64` (not `usize`)
138	        /// because the value is serialized into the persisted log — a
139	        /// 32-bit consumer must read what a 64-bit producer wrote.
140	        original_count: u64,
141	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.

2	//!
3	//! `Session` models conversation persistence as an **append-only event
4	//! log**, not a flat message list. The event-log shape gives evals
5	//! (deterministic replay), durability (Temporal/Restate-style event
6	//! sourcing), and an audit trail for regulated deployments.

14	/// Conversation persistence as an append-only event log.
15	///
16	/// See the *Sessions* concept page for the rationale.
17	///
18	/// # Example
19	///
20	/// ```
21	/// use async_trait::async_trait;
22	/// use paigasus_helikon_core::{
23	///     ConversationSnapshot, SequenceId, Session, SessionError, SessionEvent,
24	/// };
25	///
26	/// struct MemorySession;
27	///
28	/// #[async_trait]
29	/// impl Session for MemorySession {
30	///     async fn append(
31	///         &self,
32	///         _events: &[SessionEvent],
33	///     ) -> Result<(), SessionError> {
34	///         Ok(())
35	///     }
36	///
37	///     async fn events(
38	///         &self,
39	///         _since: Option<SequenceId>,
40	///     ) -> Result<Vec<SessionEvent>, SessionError> {
41	///         Ok(Vec::new())
42	///     }
43	///
44	///     async fn snapshot(&self) -> Result<ConversationSnapshot, SessionError> {
45	///         Ok(ConversationSnapshot::default())
46	///     }
47	/// }
48	/// ```
49	#[async_trait]
50	pub trait Session: Send + Sync {
51	    /// Append events to the log.
52	    async fn append(&self, events: &[SessionEvent]) -> Result<(), SessionError>;
53	
54	    /// Read events from the log, optionally only those after `since`.
55	    async fn events(&self, since: Option<SequenceId>) -> Result<Vec<SessionEvent>, SessionError>;
56	
57	    /// Compute (or read) a [`ConversationSnapshot`] projection of the log.
58	    async fn snapshot(&self) -> Result<ConversationSnapshot, SessionError>;
59	}

71	    /// A user-authored message.
72	    ///

74	    /// variant) so downstream tests and fixtures can construct variants
75	    /// by struct-init to pin a deterministic `ts`. Don't tighten this to
76	    /// per-variant `#[non_exhaustive]`.
77	    UserMessage {
78	        /// Content blocks of the message.
79	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
80	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
81	        ts: Timestamp,
82	    },
83	    /// An assistant-authored message attributed to a named agent.
84	    AssistantMessage {
85	        /// Content blocks of the message.
86	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
87	        /// Name of the emitting [`crate::Agent`]. `String` (not `Option`)

89	        /// appending to the log.
90	        agent: String,
91	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
92	        ts: Timestamp,
93	    },
94	    /// The runner invoked a tool.
95	    ToolCalled {
96	        /// Provider-assigned call identifier.
97	        call_id: String,
98	        /// Tool name.
99	        name: String,
100	        /// JSON arguments.
101	        args: serde_json::Value,
102	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
103	        ts: Timestamp,
104	    },
105	    /// The tool returned.

107	        /// Matching call identifier.

109	        /// Content blocks of the tool's output (Anthropic permits
