111	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
112	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
113	        ts: Timestamp,
114	    },
115	    /// Control transferred from one agent to another.
116	    HandoffOccurred {
117	        /// Outgoing agent name.
118	        from: String,
119	        /// Incoming agent name.
120	        to: String,
121	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
122	        ts: Timestamp,
123	    },

125	    ///

132	    /// observation-only in the event log; the model sees the summary text

135	        /// LLM-produced summary.

139	        /// 32-bit consumer must read what a 64-bit producer wrote.
140	        original_count: u64,
141	        /// Wall-clock instant the event was recorded. UTC, nanosecond precision.
142	        ts: Timestamp,
143	    },
144	}

Four steps run outside the diff before the PR is mergeable. Two are passive checks (§4.1 token, §4.2 names); two are diagnostic/mutating (§4.3 baseline dry-run, §4.4 stub pre-publish). Linear order matters — see the rollout sequence in §4.4.

### 4.1 `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` repo secret

`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml` already wires `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}` into the `release` step (since SMA-307). The secret has never been set because `publish = false` made it unused. Sven needs to:

1. Create a crates.io API token at <https://crates.io/settings/tokens> with scopes: `publish-new`, `publish-update`. (Least privilege — release-plz never needs to yank or change ownership. If we ever need to yank, do it from a separate short-lived token or the web UI as a deliberate human action.)
2. Add it to the repo as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (Repository secrets, not Environment secrets).

The token is bound to Sven's crates.io account; first publishes will create him as the owner of each crate. He can later `cargo owner --add github:paigasus:publishers` (or whatever org/team structure we end up with) if we want shared ownership.

61	
62	No changes to: any non-test `src/`, the six crates' versions, `Cargo.lock` (it'll regenerate naturally), `ci.yml`, `msrv.yml`, `audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `release-plz.yml`, `deny.toml`, `dependabot.yml`, `.gitattributes`, or scripts.
63	
64	## 4. Preflight (must happen before merge)
65	
66	Four steps run outside the diff before the PR is mergeable. Two are passive checks (§4.1 token, §4.2 names); two are diagnostic/mutating (§4.3 baseline dry-run, §4.4 stub pre-publish). Linear order matters — see the rollout sequence in §4.4.
67	
68	### 4.1 `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` repo secret
69	
70	`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml` already wires `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}` into the `release` step (since SMA-307). The secret has never been set because `publish = false` made it unused. Sven needs to:
71	
72	1. Create a crates.io API token at <https://crates.io/settings/tokens> with scopes: `publish-new`, `publish-update`. (Least privilege — release-plz never needs to yank or change ownership. If we ever need to yank, do it from a separate short-lived token or the web UI as a deliberate human action.)
73	2. Add it to the repo as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (Repository secrets, not Environment secrets).
74	
75	The token is bound to Sven's crates.io account; first publishes will create him as the owner of each crate. He can later `cargo owner --add github:paigasus:publishers` (or whatever org/team structure we end up with) if we want shared ownership.
76	
77	### 4.2 Name availability
78	
79	Verify each of the 6 to-be-published names returns 404 from crates.io:
80	
81	```bash
82	for name in paigasus-helikon paigasus-helikon-core paigasus-helikon-macros \
83	            paigasus-helikon-providers-openai paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic \
84	            paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite; do
85	  status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$name")
86	  printf '%s -> %s\n' "$name" "$status"
87	done
88	```
89	
90	Expected output: six `404` lines. If any returns `200`, halt — the name is taken; we'll need to either negotiate ownership or rename. (Given the niche-ness of "paigasus", a conflict is unlikely but not impossible.)
91	
92	Repeat the check for each of the 7 stubs (`-mcp`, `-tools`, `-evals`, `-runtime-tokio`, `-runtime-axum`, `-runtime-temporal`, `-runtime-agentcore`). Same expected output. The stub names need claiming too because of §4.4 below.
93	
94	### 4.3 `cargo publish --dry-run` diagnostic baseline
95	
96	Run dry-runs on all 13 crates against current `main` (no §5 changes, no §4.4 publishes yet):
97	
98	```bash
99	for crate in paigasus-helikon-core paigasus-helikon-macros \
100	             paigasus-helikon-providers-openai paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic \
101	             paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite paigasus-helikon \
102	             paigasus-helikon-mcp paigasus-helikon-tools paigasus-helikon-evals \
103	             paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum \
104	             paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore; do
105	  echo "=== $crate ==="
106	  cargo publish --dry-run -p "$crate" --allow-dirty 2>&1 | tail -6
107	done
108	```
109	
110	**Expected** baseline (verified locally 2026-05-28 during spec writing):
111	
112	| Crate | Result | Why |
113	|---|---|---|
114	| `-core` | ✅ pass | No internal deps |
115	| `-macros` | ❌ fails on `paigasus-helikon` | dev-dep cycle — §5.5 fixes |
116	| `-providers-openai`, `-providers-anthropic`, `-sessions-sqlite` | ❌ fail on `paigasus-helikon-core` | Resolves after release-plz publishes core post-merge |
117	| facade | ❌ fails on `paigasus-helikon-core` (and would then fail on stubs) | Resolves after release-plz publishes core, deps already-published stubs from §4.4 |
118	| 7 stubs | ✅ pass | No internal deps; this is what makes §4.4 possible |

Mitigation:

- A GitHub environment `release` with a deployment branch policy that allows
  only the `main` branch (custom branch policy, one entry: `main`). No required
  reviewers, because the release must stay automatic.
- The three secrets `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`
  and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` move from repository secrets to environment
  secrets of `release`. They are used only in `release-plz.yml`.
- The `release-plz` job sets `environment: release`.
- The environment and its branch policy are configuration as code: extend
  `scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` to create or update the environment
  idempotently. Document it where `CONTRIBUTING.md` describes "Repo
  configuration".
- A workflow on another branch then cannot read these secrets. The job on `main`
  reads the environment secrets, which override repository secrets of the same
  name.

Secret values cannot be read back from GitHub, so Sven sets the environment
secrets by hand. Recommended: use the move to rotate. Make a new App private key
and a new crates.io token (publish-update scope), set them on the environment,
and revoke the old ones after the first good run.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The design is sound. It uses the two-PR split, uses only core API that is already on crates.io, and keeps the path-only dev-dependencies. But the spec has the wrong model of *when* release-plz publishes, and it does not check whether the crates.io token can publish a crate name that does not exist yet. Fix the BLOCKER before the merge, and correct the MAJOR items in the spec text. No redesign is needed.

I could only read files. I did not run cargo, release-plz, git or the network.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
- **The token may not be able to publish a new crate name** - The testkit name was never claimed (spec lines 43-44). A first publish of a new name needs the crates.io `publish-new` scope. The SMA-745 design told Sven to rotate to "a new crates.io token (publish-update scope)" when the secret moved to the `release` environment (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-sma-745-release-plz-workflow-ref-403-design.md:152-155`). SMA-385 already rated a missing `publish-new` scope as a risk (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-28-sma-385-lift-publish-false-design.md:72,376`). The last brand-new crates were `-providers-litellm` and `-runtime-actix`, in July/August 2026. Both came before that rotation, so the current token has never published a new crate. The spec says the token "does not change" (line 31-32) but never checks its scope. | Why it matters: if `cargo publish` gets a 403, the `release` step fails. The `release-pr` step has no `if:` (`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml:51-62`), so it is skipped. Every later push to `main` tries the testkit again and fails again. The release PR then stops updating, and the SMA-803 core release stalls too. This is the anti-goal on spec line 36. | Suggested fix: add a preflight step before the merge. Sven opens crates.io/settings/tokens and confirms two things. First, the token's endpoint scopes include `publish-new`. Second, its crate scope is empty or a pattern that matches `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` (for example `paigasus-helikon*`). If not, rotate the `release` environment secret first. Add the same note to the ascend recipe in `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:15-19`.

### MAJOR
- **The testkit publishes when PR 1 merges, not when the release PR merges** - `release-plz.toml` has no `release_always` key, so it defaults to true. `release-plz.yml:51-57` runs `release` before `release-pr` on every push. CLAUDE.md says that a PR that bumps its own version "publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR". The brand-new crates `-sessions-postgres` and `-sessions-redis` prove this: their CHANGELOGs start at 0.1.1 and have no 0.1.0 entry (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/CHANGELOG.md:52`). Spec lines 55-57 ("stays green until the release PR merges"), 104-105 and 132-134 ("the release PR shows the testkit at 0.1.0") are therefore wrong. Spec line 58-59 says the opposite, so the spec also contradicts itself. | Why it matters: the person who checks the merge looks in the wrong place. If the testkit is not in the release PR, they can wrongly decide that something failed and hand-bump or revert it. The SMA-745 rule (do not let a workflow-changing PR merge during a release-plz run, runbook line 73) now applies to the merge of PR 1 itself. | Suggested fix: rewrite "Verification for PR 1". Check the release-plz run of the PR 1 merge commit for four results: crates.io lists 0.1.0, the tag `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit-v0.1.0` exists, a non-draft GitHub release exists, and the gap report says "no gaps". Merge PR 1 only when no release-plz run is queued and no PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` is about to merge.
- **There is no plan for a failed first publish** - Many causes can fail the first publish: the token scope, a crates.io outage, a failed verify, or someone else taking the name. In each case the stall described in the BLOCKER happens. `release-plz.yml` has no `workflow_dispatch` (lines 3-5). | Why it matters: there is no written way to unblock releases, and SMA-803 is waiting. | Suggested fix: add an "If the first publish fails" section. (1) Read the run log. (2) Fix the cause. (3) Re-run the failed run, and confirm that a new attempt really started (`gh run rerun` can exit 0 and not start a run). (4) If the cause cannot be fixed quickly, land a `chore(release)` PR that puts back `publish = false` and the `release = false` block. That unblocks `release-pr`.
- **PR 2 has an unstated gate: testkit 0.1.0 must already be on crates.io** - Suppose PR 2 merges while 0.1.0 is still unpublished, for example because PR 1's publish failed. Then the `release` step publishes 0.1.0 with code that uses `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred`. `cargo publish --verify` builds that code against the registry core, which does not have the variant yet. That is the SMA-321 deadlock (`docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:25`). | Why it matters: PR 2 would cause the deadlock that the two-PR split is meant to avoid. | Suggested fix: in "Design: PR 2", add: "Merge only after crates.io lists `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` 0.1.0, and after SMA-803 is on `main`."
- **External consumers will get two core versions** - The testkit's public API exposes core types: `F: Fn() -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = Arc<dyn Session>>` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit/src/lib.rs:42-46,152-156`). When core makes a breaking bump, release-plz gives its dependents only a patch bump. For example, core went 0.4.1 to 0.5.0 (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/CHANGELOG.md:137`) and sqlite went only 0.1.7 to 0.1.8 on the same day (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite/CHANGELOG.md:124`). So after the next core minor, a testkit 0.1.x patch will require the new core. A host that has `core = "0.5"` and `testkit = "0.1"` then resolves two core versions. Cargo does not refuse this, because the two versions are semver-incompatible, so the error comes at compile time: "expected `dyn paigasus_helikon_core::Session`, found `dyn paigasus_helikon_core::Session`". The spec's stability note (lines 97-100) covers only new sub-tests. | Why it matters: the host that uses the testkit implements `Session` against core directly, so it is the consumer most exposed to this error. Core has had five breaking bumps in six months. | Suggested fix: (a) In the README, say that the testkit and your crate must resolve to the same core version, and show `cargo tree -d -i paigasus-helikon-core` as the check. (b) Add a release rule: when a release PR carries a core minor bump, hand-edit the testkit to its next minor in that release PR. CONTRIBUTING.md:369-371 allows such edits. (c) In "Approaches", weigh one alternative: ship the suite as an optional feature or module of core. That removes the version skew by design. Its cost is a core change and a tokio dependency behind a feature.

### MINOR
- **No CHANGELOG for 0.1.0** - Because the release step publishes 0.1.0 on the merge, `release-pr` never proposes 0.1.0, and nothing writes a CHANGELOG for it. The GitHub release for 0.1.0 will then most likely have an empty body. I base this on how release-plz handles a missing changelog (it logs a warning and uses an empty body) and on the precedent crates that have no 0.1.0 section. I did not run release-plz to confirm it. The gap-report recovery text also tells the operator to use `${dir}/CHANGELOG.md` (`scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:350,363`), and that file will not exist. | Suggested fix: write `CHANGELOG.md` by hand in PR 1, with `## [Unreleased]` and a `## [0.1.0]` section. The precedent is `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/CHANGELOG.md:196-207`.
- **The gap-report reasoning is wrong** - When a crate does not exist on crates.io, the API returns 404 and the script reports "could not check" (`scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:235-237`). It does not report "not a gap". The self-test case `crates-404` expects exit 2 (`scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh:314-316`). On a green release step this is only a `::warning::`, so the result does not change, only the reason. | Suggested fix: correct spec lines 54-57.
- **The PR title type is not given** - PRs are squash-merged, so only the PR title reaches `main`. The branch commit types in spec item 6 never reach release-plz. The CLAUDE.md bootstrap rule asks for `chore`/`docs` when a change edits `release-plz.toml`. The scopes `sessions` (`.github/workflows/pr-title.yml:59`, `.versionrc:18`) and `release` (`pr-title.yml:65`) are valid. The type has no bump effect here, because the only packaged path that changes is the testkit, and it is already published when `release-pr` compares. | Suggested fix: give the exact title, for example `chore(sessions): SMA-805 publish the sessions testkit to crates.io`.
- **The doc sweep misses some places** - `docs/book/src/introduction.md:19` ("Twenty crates are published"). The `docs/book/src/reference/api-docs.md:7-26` "Published crates" list needs a testkit bullet; the spec names only line 32. The `README.md:35-50` crate roster needs a testkit bullet. `docs/book/src/reference/crates.md:17`, `:43` and `:51` ("Like `-sessions-testkit`, all three are intentional non-published…"). `docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md:346-347` still calls Postgres and Redis "forthcoming". The "all twenty-one" claim is correct for `crates/`: the directory has 21 members, and the three unpublished members are outside it (root `Cargo.toml:3`). | Suggested fix: add these places to item 5.
- **A comment in `release-plz.toml` will point at nothing** - `release-plz.toml:38-40` says "the same publish=false / release=false pair as the testkit above". After the block is removed, "the testkit above" does not exist. The "Stubs: pre-published at 0.0.0" comment at `:29-32` does not describe any of the three blocks that remain. | Suggested fix: rewrite both comments as one comment about internal test-harness members.
- **Two dependencies are unused, and Cargo.lock is not listed** - Neither `src/lib.rs` nor `tests/memory.rs` uses `async-trait` or `futures-util` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit/Cargo.toml:17-18`). After the publish, every consumer compiles them. The `Cargo.lock` entry also changes from 0.0.0 to 0.1.0 (`Cargo.lock:4529-4538`). | Suggested fix: remove the two dependencies before the first publish, and add `Cargo.lock` to the change set.
- **The README guidance is partly wrong and partly missing** - The `multi_thread` reason in spec line 92-94 is wrong. `tests/memory.rs:8` uses the default current-thread `#[tokio::test]` and passes, because `tokio::spawn` works on that runtime. The real requirements are these. `run_all` must run inside a Tokio runtime, because `lib.rs:117` calls `tokio::spawn` and panics outside one. `multi_thread` is only recommended, so that the 16 writers really run in parallel. The consumer needs its own `tokio` dev-dependency with `macros` and `rt-multi-thread`. | Suggested fix: write these points in the README. For a shared database, also show how to give each call a fresh session: a process id plus a counter (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/tests/conformance.rs:20-31`).
- **The doctest choice is unclear** - `MemorySession` is a public core export (`tests/memory.rs:4`), so the doctest can use it. But rustdoc compiles doctests without `--test`, so a doctest whose body is a `#[tokio::test]` function compiles and never runs. And if the README is pulled into the crate docs with `include_str!`, lines hidden with `# ` still show on crates.io. | Suggested fix: pick one form. Either use a crate-doc example with `#[tokio::main(flavor = "multi_thread")] async fn main()` that really calls `run_all`, or use `include_str!` with no hidden lines.
- **PR 2 cannot make its assertions as written** - `SessionEvent` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs:67`), `ConversationSnapshot` (`:554`) and `Item` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/item.rs:18`) do not derive `PartialEq`. The checks "exact field values" and "`snapshot()` equals `project(...)`" therefore need one of two things. One is a core derive, which breaks the non-goal and collides with the SMA-803/804 core work. The other is a `serde_json::Value` comparison, which needs a new `serde_json` dependency in the testkit. | Suggested fix: specify the `serde_json` comparison. Keep whole-second `ts` values, as `lib.rs:14` does. An external backend that stores `timestamptz` keeps only microseconds, so a nanosecond-exact check would fail.
- **No check from outside the workspace** - `cargo package` proves that the tarball compiles. It does not prove that a crate outside the workspace can call `run_all`. | Suggested fix: add a scratch crate outside the workspace. It depends on `target/package/paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit-0.1.0` by path and on core from the registry, and it runs the README example.

### QUESTIONS

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The design is sound. It uses the two-PR split, uses only core API that is already on crates.io, and keeps the path-only dev-dependencies. But the spec has the wrong model of *when* release-plz publishes, and it does not check whether the crates.io token can publish a crate name that does not exist yet. Fix the BLOCKER before the merge, and correct the MAJOR items in the spec text. No redesign is needed.

I could only read files. I did not run cargo, release-plz, git or the network.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
- **The token may not be able to publish a new crate name** - The testkit name was never claimed (spec lines 43-44). A first publish of a new name needs the crates.io `publish-new` scope. The SMA-745 design told Sven to rotate to "a new crates.io token (publish-update scope)" when the secret moved to the `release` environment (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-sma-745-release-plz-workflow-ref-403-design.md:152-155`). SMA-385 already rated a missing `publish-new` scope as a risk (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-28-sma-385-lift-publish-false-design.md:72,376`). The last brand-new crates were `-providers-litellm` and `-runtime-actix`, in July/August 2026. Both came before that rotation, so the current token has never published a new crate. The spec says the token "does not change" (line 31-32) but never checks its scope. | Why it matters: if `cargo publish` gets a 403, the `release` step fails. The `release-pr` step has no `if:` (`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml:51-62`), so it is skipped. Every later push to `main` tries the testkit again and fails again. The release PR then stops updating, and the SMA-803 core release stalls too. This is the anti-goal on spec line 36. | Suggested fix: add a preflight step before the merge. Sven opens crates.io/settings/tokens and confirms two things. First, the token's endpoint scopes include `publish-new`. Second, its crate scope is empty or a pattern that matches `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` (for example `paigasus-helikon*`). If not, rotate the `release` environment secret first. Add the same note to the ascend recipe in `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:15-19`.

### MAJOR
- **The testkit publishes when PR 1 merges, not when the release PR merges** - `release-plz.toml` has no `release_always` key, so it defaults to true. `release-plz.yml:51-57` runs `release` before `release-pr` on every push. CLAUDE.md says that a PR that bumps its own version "publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR". The brand-new crates `-sessions-postgres` and `-sessions-redis` prove this: their CHANGELOGs start at 0.1.1 and have no 0.1.0 entry (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/CHANGELOG.md:52`). Spec lines 55-57 ("stays green until the release PR merges"), 104-105 and 132-134 ("the release PR shows the testkit at 0.1.0") are therefore wrong. Spec line 58-59 says the opposite, so the spec also contradicts itself. | Why it matters: the person who checks the merge looks in the wrong place. If the testkit is not in the release PR, they can wrongly decide that something failed and hand-bump or revert it. The SMA-745 rule (do not let a workflow-changing PR merge during a release-plz run, runbook line 73) now applies to the merge of PR 1 itself. | Suggested fix: rewrite "Verification for PR 1". Check the release-plz run of the PR 1 merge commit for four results: crates.io lists 0.1.0, the tag `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit-v0.1.0` exists, a non-draft GitHub release exists, and the gap report says "no gaps". Merge PR 1 only when no release-plz run is queued and no PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` is about to merge.
- **There is no plan for a failed first publish** - Many causes can fail the first publish: the token scope, a crates.io outage, a failed verify, or someone else taking the name. In each case the stall described in the BLOCKER happens. `release-plz.yml` has no `workflow_dispatch` (lines 3-5). | Why it matters: there is no written way to unblock releases, and SMA-803 is waiting. | Suggested fix: add an "If the first publish fails" section. (1) Read the run log. (2) Fix the cause. (3) Re-run the failed run, and confirm that a new attempt really started (`gh run rerun` can exit 0 and not start a run). (4) If the cause cannot be fixed quickly, land a `chore(release)` PR that puts back `publish = false` and the `release = false` block. That unblocks `release-pr`.
- **PR 2 has an unstated gate: testkit 0.1.0 must already be on crates.io** - Suppose PR 2 merges while 0.1.0 is still unpublished, for example because PR 1's publish failed. Then the `release` step publishes 0.1.0 with code that uses `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred`. `cargo publish --verify` builds that code against the registry core, which does not have the variant yet. That is the SMA-321 deadlock (`docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:25`). | Why it matters: PR 2 would cause the deadlock that the two-PR split is meant to avoid. | Suggested fix: in "Design: PR 2", add: "Merge only after crates.io lists `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` 0.1.0, and after SMA-803 is on `main`."
- **External consumers will get two core versions** - The testkit's public API exposes core types: `F: Fn() -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = Arc<dyn Session>>` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit/src/lib.rs:42-46,152-156`). When core makes a breaking bump, release-plz gives its dependents only a patch bump. For example, core went 0.4.1 to 0.5.0 (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/CHANGELOG.md:137`) and sqlite went only 0.1.7 to 0.1.8 on the same day (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite/CHANGELOG.md:124`). So after the next core minor, a testkit 0.1.x patch will require the new core. A host that has `core = "0.5"` and `testkit = "0.1"` then resolves two core versions. Cargo does not refuse this, because the two versions are semver-incompatible, so the error comes at compile time: "expected `dyn paigasus_helikon_core::Session`, found `dyn paigasus_helikon_core::Session`". The spec's stability note (lines 97-100) covers only new sub-tests. | Why it matters: the host that uses the testkit implements `Session` against core directly, so it is the consumer most exposed to this error. Core has had five breaking bumps in six months. | Suggested fix: (a) In the README, say that the testkit and your crate must resolve to the same core version, and show `cargo tree -d -i paigasus-helikon-core` as the check. (b) Add a release rule: when a release PR carries a core minor bump, hand-edit the testkit to its next minor in that release PR. CONTRIBUTING.md:369-371 allows such edits. (c) In "Approaches", weigh one alternative: ship the suite as an optional feature or module of core. That removes the version skew by design. Its cost is a core change and a tokio dependency behind a feature.

### MINOR
- **No CHANGELOG for 0.1.0** - Because the release step publishes 0.1.0 on the merge, `release-pr` never proposes 0.1.0, and nothing writes a CHANGELOG for it. The GitHub release for 0.1.0 will then most likely have an empty body. I base this on how release-plz handles a missing changelog (it logs a warning and uses an empty body) and on the precedent crates that have no 0.1.0 section. I did not run release-plz to confirm it. The gap-report recovery text also tells the operator to use `${dir}/CHANGELOG.md` (`scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:350,363`), and that file will not exist. | Suggested fix: write `CHANGELOG.md` by hand in PR 1, with `## [Unreleased]` and a `## [0.1.0]` section. The precedent is `crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/CHANGELOG.md:196-207`.
- **The gap-report reasoning is wrong** - When a crate does not exist on crates.io, the API returns 404 and the script reports "could not check" (`scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:235-237`). It does not report "not a gap". The self-test case `crates-404` expects exit 2 (`scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh:314-316`). On a green release step this is only a `::warning::`, so the result does not change, only the reason. | Suggested fix: correct spec lines 54-57.
- **The PR title type is not given** - PRs are squash-merged, so only the PR title reaches `main`. The branch commit types in spec item 6 never reach release-plz. The CLAUDE.md bootstrap rule asks for `chore`/`docs` when a change edits `release-plz.toml`. The scopes `sessions` (`.github/workflows/pr-title.yml:59`, `.versionrc:18`) and `release` (`pr-title.yml:65`) are valid. The type has no bump effect here, because the only packaged path that changes is the testkit, and it is already published when `release-pr` compares. | Suggested fix: give the exact title, for example `chore(sessions): SMA-805 publish the sessions testkit to crates.io`.
- **The doc sweep misses some places** - `docs/book/src/introduction.md:19` ("Twenty crates are published"). The `docs/book/src/reference/api-docs.md:7-26` "Published crates" list needs a testkit bullet; the spec names only line 32. The `README.md:35-50` crate roster needs a testkit bullet. `docs/book/src/reference/crates.md:17`, `:43` and `:51` ("Like `-sessions-testkit`, all three are intentional non-published…"). `docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md:346-347` still calls Postgres and Redis "forthcoming". The "all twenty-one" claim is correct for `crates/`: the directory has 21 members, and the three unpublished members are outside it (root `Cargo.toml:3`). | Suggested fix: add these places to item 5.
- **A comment in `release-plz.toml` will point at nothing** - `release-plz.toml:38-40` says "the same publish=false / release=false pair as the testkit above". After the block is removed, "the testkit above" does not exist. The "Stubs: pre-published at 0.0.0" comment at `:29-32` does not describe any of the three blocks that remain. | Suggested fix: rewrite both comments as one comment about internal test-harness members.
- **Two dependencies are unused, and Cargo.lock is not listed** - Neither `src/lib.rs` nor `tests/memory.rs` uses `async-trait` or `futures-util` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit/Cargo.toml:17-18`). After the publish, every consumer compiles them. The `Cargo.lock` entry also changes from 0.0.0 to 0.1.0 (`Cargo.lock:4529-4538`). | Suggested fix: remove the two dependencies before the first publish, and add `Cargo.lock` to the change set.
- **The README guidance is partly wrong and partly missing** - The `multi_thread` reason in spec line 92-94 is wrong. `tests/memory.rs:8` uses the default current-thread `#[tokio::test]` and passes, because `tokio::spawn` works on that runtime. The real requirements are these. `run_all` must run inside a Tokio runtime, because `lib.rs:117` calls `tokio::spawn` and panics outside one. `multi_thread` is only recommended, so that the 16 writers really run in parallel. The consumer needs its own `tokio` dev-dependency with `macros` and `rt-multi-thread`. | Suggested fix: write these points in the README. For a shared database, also show how to give each call a fresh session: a process id plus a counter (`crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres/tests/conformance.rs:20-31`).
- **The doctest choice is unclear** - `MemorySession` is a public core export (`tests/memory.rs:4`), so the doctest can use it. But rustdoc compiles doctests without `--test`, so a doctest whose body is a `#[tokio::test]` function compiles and never runs. And if the README is pulled into the crate docs with `include_str!`, lines hidden with `# ` still show on crates.io. | Suggested fix: pick one form. Either use a crate-doc example with `#[tokio::main(flavor = "multi_thread")] async fn main()` that really calls `run_all`, or use `include_str!` with no hidden lines.
- **PR 2 cannot make its assertions as written** - `SessionEvent` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs:67`), `ConversationSnapshot` (`:554`) and `Item` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/item.rs:18`) do not derive `PartialEq`. The checks "exact field values" and "`snapshot()` equals `project(...)`" therefore need one of two things. One is a core derive, which breaks the non-goal and collides with the SMA-803/804 core work. The other is a `serde_json::Value` comparison, which needs a new `serde_json` dependency in the testkit. | Suggested fix: specify the `serde_json` comparison. Keep whole-second `ts` values, as `lib.rs:14` does. An external backend that stores `timestamptz` keeps only microseconds, so a nanosecond-exact check would fail.
- **No check from outside the workspace** - `cargo package` proves that the tarball compiles. It does not prove that a crate outside the workspace can call `run_all`. | Suggested fix: add a scratch crate outside the workspace. It depends on `target/package/paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit-0.1.0` by path and on core from the registry, and it runs the README example.
